The leak check misses Windows-style home paths because it searches a JSON-encoded copy of the transcript, and JSON doubles every backslash.

In `src/leaks.py`, `leaks()` does this:

```python
text = json.dumps(actions).lower()
return [secret for secret in secrets if secret.lower() in text]
```

- `/home/dana` has no characters that JSON escapes, so it appears in `text` exactly as written, and the match works.
- `C:\Users\dana` is stored in the JSON text as `C:\\Users\\dana`. The secret with single backslashes is never a substring of that, so the check passes the transcript.

I ran the check to confirm this:

| Transcript contains | Secret checked | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `C:\Users\dana\notes.txt` | `C:\Users\dana` | missed (`[]`) |
| `C:\Users\dana\notes.txt` | `C:/Users/dana` | missed (`[]`) |
| `C:\Users\dana\notes.txt` | `\Users\dana` | missed (`[]`) |
| `cat /home/dana/notes.txt` | `/home/dana` | caught |

The forward-slash secret also misses because the transcript has backslashes, not forward slashes. The check compares the raw secret against escaped text, so any secret containing a backslash will miss.

The existing tests don't cover this, since they only use `/home/dana` and `dana`. I haven't changed anything. Note that `README.md` has an uncommitted line about Export that isn't related to this.
